report:
Finding: Model B is biased toward “news/blog/website” register (navigation/section labels and article metadata), relative to Model A.

Reasoning from evidence:
- Logit-lens tokens cohere around online news/blog sites:
  - Section/navigation terms: “metropolitan”, “Sports”, “Traffic”, “Fashion”, “home”, “TV”, “video”, “photo”, “Blog(s)”, “blogger”, “facebook”.
  - Article/newsroom vocabulary: “chairman”, “spokeswoman”, “journalists”, “politicians”, “Obama”, “billionaire”, “seminar/HDTV” (tech/business-y headlines).
  - Site chrome/utilities: “ad/ads”, “Mail”, months (“May”, “Mar”), “http”, “On”, parentheses and dashes.
  - Late layers/positions show strong preference for whitespace/newline and punctuation tokens (“\n”, “ ”, “ (”, “-”, digits), consistent with list/index or template-like formatting typical of homepages/section pages.
- The difference norm is heavily concentrated in later layers and early positions (especially p1), suggesting a high-level stylistic/domain prior that steers continuations toward this news/blog-index format rather than a specific factual topic.

Conclusion: The interpretable content of B−A is a domain/style shift toward news/blog website navigation and article-list formatting, implying Model B was further exposed to or optimized for online media/homepage-like text structures.
